explanation: The theorem says: if an affine point (x, y) is p-torsion for an odd prime p, then x is a root of the division polynomial preΨ p. The key step in its proof, `WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.nsmul_some_eq_zero_iff_eval_prePsi`, is a lemma of the library itself (it is imported from `Theorems.Thm_WeierstrassCurve_Affine_Point_nsmul_some_eq_zero_iff_eval_prePsi`), not of Mathlib. The only Mathlib lemma the proof uses is `preΨ_ofNat`, a rewriting lemma. I grepped the Mathlib elliptic-curve directory for preΨ, ΨSq, ψ and Φ. They appear only in DivisionPolynomial/Basic.lean, DivisionPolynomial/Degree.lean, VariableChange.lean and Affine/Formula.lean. I also searched for combinations of nsmul/smul with preΨ and found none. In this Mathlib version I found nothing linking division polynomials to n-torsion points.
